info.bio:
Declan Patrick MacManus nacido en Londres el 25 de agosto de 1954, conocido como Elvis Costello, es un músico, cantante y compositor británico.

Se inició en la escena pub-rock londinense a mitad de los 70 desde donde vio llegar como observador privilegiado la New Wave y el punk, movimientos con los que se asoció.

En 1975 McManus llevaba una aparente vida convencional, casado y con hijo, y empleándose en diferentes trabajos administrativos. No obstante, componía y movía sus maquetas hasta que la independiente Stiff Records le contrató; Jack Riviera, director del sello, le propuso una identificación artística más sugerente, combinando el nombre de Elvis Presley y su segundo apellido materno: Elvis Costello ya era una realidad.

El disruptivo 1977 marca la carrera de Costello: a su fichaje por Stiff a inicios de año, le sigue la edición de su primer single Less than zero en abril, y de Alison en marzo, debutando en larga duración en verano con My aim is true, con un significativo éxito de críticas y un moderado éxito comercial (puesto 14 en el Reino Unido, entrando el el Top40 en Estados Unidos). La portada con un Costello con Fender Jazzmaster en ristre, enormes gafas de pasta, piernas en cuña embutidas en pantalón pitillo, ecos estéticos al punk y a Buddy Holly y pose desafiante era una declaración de intenciones. La banda que acompañó la grabación fueron los americanos Clover, conjunto que en aquella época practicaba el country/root y que con el tiempo se convertiría en Huey Lewis and The News: ese mismo verano, Costello reclutó a lo que sería su banda estable, The Attractions, formadada por Steve Nieve al piano, Bruce Thomas al bajo y Pete Thomas a la batería. El otoño participaría en la Stiff Live Package, con otros grupos del sello como Ian Dury, Wreckless Eric y Nick Lowe. A final de año Jack Riviera deja Stiff para fundar Radar Records a donde se llevaría a Lowe y Costello, publicando su último single Watching the detectives (grabado con el bajista y batería de Graham Parker and The Rumours) a final de año.

En los dos años siguientes publicó con el nuevo sello y la nueva banda This year's model', otra colección de singles como fue el su debut, con un estilo igual de urgente e intenso pero más crudo y directo, acaso fruto de la escena punk vigente y desligado del pub-rock setentero y músicos de country-rock con los que grabó My aim is true y Armed Forces. Con este último álbum pretendería y alcanzaría un reconocimiento comercial más amplio (el álbum y primer single Oliver's Army lograría el número dos de las listas británicas, mientras que el albúm entraría en el Top10 Estados Unidos, no así ninguno de sus singles). Armed Forces es un disco más complejo y variado musicalmente, tanto en tiempos, estilos y orquestación, igual de irónico y quizá más trabajado en cuanto a letras, y deja entrever lo que será la carrera posterior del Costello maduro de las siguientes décadas.

Costello cierra los años 70 como productor, dejando su impronta en el disco debut y homónimo de The Specials.

Una de sus canciones "Less Than Zero",sirve de titulo a la primera novela del escritor norteamericano Bret Easton Ellis la cual es una trepidante aventura de jovenes californianos adinerados marcada por el sexo,las drogas y el buen vino.
Ademas esta casado con la arrolladora cantante de jazz Diana Krall de la cual tiene dos hijos. . User-contributed text is available under the Creative Commons By-SA License; additional terms may apply.

Se inició en la escena pub rock londinense a mitad de los 70 desde donde vio llegar como observador privilegiado la new wave y el punk, movimientos con los que se asoció.

La revista Rolling Stone lo reconoció en el 2012 como uno de los 100 mejores artistas de todos los tiempos, ubicándolo en el puesto 80.[2]​

En 1975 McManus llevaba una aparente vida convencional, casado y con hijo, y empleándose en diferentes trabajos administrativos. No obstante, componía y movía sus maquetas hasta que la independiente Stiff Records le contrató; Jack Riviera, director del sello, le propuso una identificación artística más sugerente, combinando el nombre de Elvis Presley y su apellido materno: Elvis Costello ya era una realidad.

La banda que acompañó la grabación fueron los americanos Clover, conjunto que en aquella época practicaba el country-rock y que con el tiempo parte del mismo se convertiría en Huey Lewis and The News: ese mismo verano, Costello reclutó a lo que sería su banda estable, The Attractions, formada por Steve Nieve al piano, Bruce Thomas al bajo y Pete Thomas a la batería. El otoño participaría en la Stiff Live Package, con otros grupos del sello como Ian Dury, Wreckless Eric y Nick Lowe. A final de año Jack Riviera deja Stiff para fundar Radar Records a donde se llevaría a Lowe y Costello, publicando su último sencillo Watching the detectives (grabado con el bajista y batería de Graham Parker and The Rumours) a final de año.

En los dos años siguientes publicó con el nuevo sello y la nueva banda This Year's Model', otra colección de singles como fue el su debut, con un estilo igual de urgente e intenso pero más crudo y directo, acaso fruto de la escena punk vigente y desligado del pub-rock setentero y músicos de country-rock con los que grabó My aim is true y Armed Forces. Con este último álbum pretendería y alcanzaría un reconocimiento comercial más amplio (el álbum y primer single Oliver's Army lograría el número dos de las listas británicas, mientras que el álbum entraría en el Top10 Estados Unidos, no así ninguno de sus singles). Armed Forces es un disco más complejo y variado musicalmente, tanto en tiempos, estilos y orquestación, igual de irónico y quizá más trabajado en cuanto a letras, y deja entrever lo que será la carrera posterior del Costello maduro de las siguientes décadas.

Costello cierra los setenta como productor, dejando su impronta en el disco debut y homónimo de The Specials. Son conocidas sus incursiones en el mundo de la música clásica como es el caso de sus obras "The Juliette Letters" y "Il Sogno". En 1999, participa en el multitudinario festival de Woodstock, dando un emotivo show en ese caótico festival.
Elvis Costello se casó con Diana Krall en diciembre de 2003 y tuvieron dos hijos gemelos el 6 de diciembre de 2006 en Nueva York, Dexter Henry Lorcan y Frank Harlan James.

En 2008 Costello presentó un programa de televisión llamado Elvis Costello with... (Elvis Costello con...), coproducido por CTV (Canadá), Channel 4 (UK) y Sundance Channel (USA). El programa desarrollaba entrevistas en profundidad a miembros destacados del negocio musical. Su primer invitado fue Elton John. El espacio televisivo tenía fines benéficos, para recaudar dinero en la lucha contra el sida en África.[3]​

podcast.title: Inspiration from Sex Pistols (December 2, 1976)
podcast.body: Declan McManus, then a computer operator, was deeply inspired by the Sex Pistols' scandalous appearance on a TV show where they used "bad words." Feeling they had "shaken up the system," he decided to quit his data entry job, picked up a guitar, and changed his name to Elvis Costello, embodying the attitude, anger, and energy he saw in the Sex Pistols. "He wanted to be involved in whatever it was that the sex pistols embodied, the attitude, the anger, the energy."

podcast.title: "Nerd Rock" Attribution and SNL Sketches (December 1977)
podcast.body: During his appearance on Saturday Night Live in December 1977, Elvis Costello, characterized by his thick glasses and powder-blue sport coat, was performing at the peak of his "angry young songwriter" phase. A writer for the show, Beats, observed his performance and coined the term "nerd rock" to describe his style, leading to the creation of the recurring "Nerds" sketches on SNL featuring Gilda Radner, Jane Curtin, and Bill Murray. "this isn't punk rock, this is nerd rock."

podcast.title: My Aim Is True (1977) – Debut Album Recorded by Clover, Who Became Huey Lewis and the News
podcast.body: Before his music career, Elvis Costello worked as a computer operator for Elizabeth Arden cosmetics, running invoices on an IBM 360 mainframe, taking occasional sick days to demo songs. When he signed to Stiff Records, he needed a backing band. An American group called Clover had just arrived in England hoping for their big break, but found themselves stranded in the middle of punk and unwanted. They needed money for plane tickets home. Elvis went to their residency at Headley Grange, told them he needed a studio band and specifically didn't need a singer, so Clover's own singer was sent to wait elsewhere while the rest of the band backed Elvis through six four-hour sessions for his debut. Clover was paid and sent back to the US, where they reinvented themselves as Huey Lewis and the News. The singer who had to hang out during the Costello sessions was Huey Lewis. "That banished singer was Huey Lewis."

podcast.title: Prolific Output and Market Dilution (1977-1986)
podcast.body: Costello released a new album every year between 1977 and 1986, a rate considered "too prolific." This rapid creation of new music meant his labels often lacked sufficient time to promote and market his albums effectively, and the music press struggled to keep up with reviews. The "glut of material" ultimately diluted his market worth and equity, even among diehard fans. "Elvis released a new album every year between 1977 and 1986."

podcast.title: Saturday Night Live Act of Defiance (December 17, 1977)
podcast.body: Elvis Costello's North American breakthrough came when he was a last-minute replacement musical guest on Saturday Night Live on December 17, 1977, after the Sex Pistols faced visa issues. NBC insisted he play his British hit "Less Than Zero" and avoid "Radio, Radio," which was critical of radio (a sensitive topic given NBC's radio station ownership). Costello feigned agreement but defiantly launched into "Radio, Radio" live on air, an "act of corporate nose thumming" that inspired thousands. "That act of defiance, that act of corporate nose thumming inspired thousands."

podcast.title: Saturday Night Live Appearance (December 1977)
podcast.body: During his performance on Saturday Night Live in December 1977, at the peak of his "angry young songwriter" phase, Elvis Costello, dressed with thick glasses and a powder blue sport coat, was observed by SNL writer Tom Davis, who famously thought, "this isn't punk rock, this is nerd rock." This moment contributed to the coining of the term "nerd rock" and directly led to the creation of the recurring "The Nerds" sketch on the show. "In December 1977, Elvis Costello appeared on Saturday Night Live. He was at the height of his angry young songwriter years, complete with his thick glasses and powder blue sport coat."

podcast.title: Saturday Night Live Stunt (1977)
podcast.body: Costello and The Attractions secured their appearance on NBC TV's *Saturday Night Live* only because the original guests, The Sex Pistols, were unable to perform due to visa issues. Columbia Records insisted Costello perform his single "Less Than Zero," but believing Americans wouldn't understand its subject matter (British fascist Oswald Mosley), Costello abruptly stopped the song after just seven seconds live on the air and switched to the then-unreleased "Radio, Radio." This act enraged SNL producer Lorne Michaels and NBC brass, leading to Costello being banned from the show for a dozen years. However, Columbia Records viewed it as excellent publicity, solidifying Costello's image as a "punk fellow traveler" and an "actual angry young man." "What Costello pulled live on the air that night became the stuff of legend."

podcast.title: Saturday Night Live Incident (December 17, 1978)
podcast.body: As a last-minute replacement for the Sex Pistols (who faced visa issues), Elvis Costello appeared on "Saturday Night Live" in December 1978. Producers explicitly asked him not to play "Radio Radio" due to NBC's ownership of radio stations and the song's critical lyrics. Costello agreed but then famously played "Radio Radio" instead of the requested song, causing a stir. "But then this is what happened on December 17, 1978... Radio Radio."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Columbus Holiday Inn Bar Fight (March 10, 1979) – Racist Remarks, Punch from Bonnie Bramlett, Career Nearly Ruined in America
podcast.body: On March 10, 1979, Elvis Costello and his entourage were drinking heavily in a bar at a Holiday Inn in Columbus, Ohio, when they encountered Stephen Stills's party. Costello made blatant racist remarks about Ray Charles and James Brown. Stephen Stills's companion Bonnie Bramlett punched Costello, a full brawl broke out, and the incident made national news. American media sided with Stills; Costello became toxic and his American career took years to recover. He later described the incident in his memoirs *Unfaithful Music and Disappearing Ink* (2015) and acknowledged it without denial or excuse. "An old barfight from 37 years ago — but there are real serious things that haven't been fixed that are not my doing or my responsibility."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Columbus, Ohio Incident (1979)
podcast.body: In the spring of 1979, during a drunken exchange at a hotel bar in Columbus, Ohio, Costello used racial slurs to insult several African American musical artists, including James Brown and Ray Charles, in front of members of Stephen Stills' band. When details of this incident were leaked to the press, his American reputation was tarnished, leading radio stations to pull the *Armed Forces* LP from rotation and causing later dates on his US tour to sell poorly. Costello, who had previously been involved in England's Rock Against Racism movement, felt foolish and expressed deep regret for the incident in later interviews, stating in 1982, "what could I do, hold up a sign that read, I really like black people?" "After Word got around that spring of an incident at a hotel bar in Columbus, Ohio between Costello and members of Stephen Stills band."

podcast.body: With his acerbic rock nerd persona, Costello was the first to establish the archetype of the "Angry Young Man" among his peers. "No one would even think to call Graham Parker an angry young man before this other, a Serbic rock nerd built that archetype first."

podcast.title: "Angry Young Men" Moniker
podcast.body: Along with Joe Jackson and Graham Parker, Elvis Costello was among a group of British singer-songwriters who emerged from Pub Rock and Powerpop, adopted a punk attitude, helped shape new wave, and were collectively tagged with the moniker "Angry Young Men." podcast.title: "Imperial Bedroom" Pazz & Jop Critics Poll
podcast.body: In 1982, Elvis Costello's album "Imperial Bedroom" topped the Pazz & Jop critics poll, an annual survey of music critics. This critical acclaim underscored the album's artistic significance and sophisticated nature, even though it performed modestly on commercial charts. "Imperial Bedroom topped the Paz and Job critics poll for 1982."

podcast.title: "Telegenically Challenged" Assessment
podcast.body: Elvis Costello is cited as an example of an artist with "superior talent" but who was considered "telegenically challenged," meaning his visual appeal did not align with the demands of the music video era. This led to him not achieving the same level of superstar status as performers like Madonna, whose looks were perceived as aligning better with the visual medium. "This explains why someone like Madonna is a superstar, but somebody like Elvis Costello, not so much."

podcast.title: Acknowledged Vocal Limitations
podcast.body: Elvis Costello has always been aware of his "serious vocal limitations," which motivated him to constantly stretch his abilities as a musician and experiment with diverse projects if he wanted to sustain his career. This self-awareness drove his extensive collaborations and genre explorations. "Elvis knows that he has serious vocal limitations, he's always known that he's need to stretch his limits as a musician if he was going to keep doing this for a living."

podcast.title: Alt Rock Radio Fixture at 35
podcast.body: By the age of 35, Elvis Costello had emerged as a consistent presence on alt rock radio, particularly with the success of singles like "Veronica" and "This Town." This positioned him as an influential figure within the developing alternative rock scene. "At age 35 Costello was emerging as an alt rock radio fixture."

podcast.title: An Artist's Artist
podcast.body: By the time of his 1989 album "Spike," Elvis Costello had established himself as one of the world's most influential singer-songwriters, especially among his peers. He became known as an "artist's artist," a figure other performers looked to for guidance and inspiration, demonstrating how to develop one's craft and grow artistically. "He had become an artist's artist. Someone other performers looked to for guidance and inspiration."

xref.title: Disastrous American Tour – January 1978
xref.body: Manager Malcolm McLaren's plan to "conquer America" with the Sex Pistols resulted in one of rock history's most disastrous road trips. Initially, the group's visa applications were denied, forcing them to cancel an important appearance on Saturday Night Live, where Elvis Costello was called in as a last-minute replacement. The drummer for Elvis Costello's performance notably wore a t-shirt that read "Thanks, milk," a sarcastic jab at Malcolm McLaren. McLaren made a bizarre miscalculation about American culture by routing the tour away from major cities and through the deep South, an area not receptive to punk rock values. "Instead, what he got was one of the most disastrous road trips in the history of rock."

xref.body: The band Clover provided backup instrumentation for Elvis Costello's debut album, *My Aim is True*, performing under the name The Shamrocks. After their work with Costello, and once he had auditioned players for his permanent group (The Attractions), Clover returned to the United States and subsequently changed their name to Huey Lewis and the News, becoming the well-known band.

xref.title: Covered Nick Lowe's Tracks

xref.title: First Canadian Band to Sign to Stiff Records – Power Pop Side of Vancouver Punk
xref.body: The Pointed Sticks formed in Vancouver in 1978, five former members overlapping with D.O.A. and the Subhumans. Their sound was more melodic and power pop-leaning than their contemporaries — five members singing harmonies was unusual in punk. Their name came from a Monty Python sketch about self-defense against pointed sticks. They became the first Canadian band to sign to Stiff Records in the UK, home to the Damned, Nick Lowe, Elvis Costello, and Ian Dury. Several strong singles and one album followed. Their relative accessibility broadened the audience for Vancouver punk. "Stiff Records, one of the groundbreaking indie labels in the UK."

xref.title: Post-Breakup Member Destinies
xref.body: After Clover broke up in 1978, its members pursued various paths. One individual joined The Doobie Brothers before eventually quitting music to become a chiropractor. Additionally, two members, along with Clover's singer (who had merely hung around during the Elvis Costello sessions), went on to form the successful band Huey Lewis and the News. xref.title: Robert Smith's Early Influences
xref.body: Robert Smith's older siblings introduced him to a diverse range of artists, including The Beatles, The Rolling Stones, Captain Beefheart, David Bowie, Jimi Hendrix, and Nick Drake. The subsequent arrival of punk rock, with bands like Sex Pistols, Ramones, and Elvis Costello, further shaped his musical direction and helped him find his artistic niche. "His older brother and sister had filled his head with beetles and stone songs, but they also subjected him to a lot of Captain B-Fart, and David Bowie, and Jimmy Hendrix and Nick Drake. And then when punk came along, it was Sex Pistols Ramones Elvis Costello. Young Robert found his niche."

xref.title: Songwriting Influence
xref.body: Nick Lowe is a highly influential songwriter, not only having hit singles of his own but also seeing several of his tracks become hits for other artists, including Elvis Costello and Johnny Cash. His talent is recognized by contemporary musicians, with Alex Turner of the Arctic Monkeys citing him as a favorite songwriter. "If you ask Alex Turner of the Arctic Monkeys who his favorite songwriter of all time is, he will tell you that one of them has got to be Nick Lowe."

xref.title: Uncredited Backing Band for Elvis Costello
xref.body: Clover was an American band that found itself broke while touring the UK. They were hired by Jake Riviera of Stiff Records to back Elvis Costello on his debut album, My Aim Is True, recording through late 1976 and early 1977 in a tiny studio in Islington, London. Due to contractual issues (another British band was already named Clover), they used the pseudonym The Sham Rocks and were never credited on the original album release. "So Riviera found a band called Clover, who had come over from America, and were pretty much broke as they tried to or the UK."
